_comment: Per-indicator AMBER/RED threshold tuning applied at score time. `default` (top-level) is the engine-wide shared multiplier applied to EVERY cut/threshold via the direction-normalized earliness transform (m<1 = fire EARLIER, m>1 = later); a per-id `multiplier` override supersedes it. Knobs: `amberMult`/`redMult` scale that band's constant PER-LEG with RAW multiply (any finite value; a NEGATIVE flips the band's sign — the only way to lift a LOW-is-bad decline band like F6 amber -2.5% up to a positive +5% level, and being independent it lets amber sit at a LARGER positive % than red so amber/red ordering holds — the sign-flip escape hatch, NOT normalized). `multiplier` is the shared per-id override for both legs, POSITIVE-ONLY (zero/negative/non-finite -> falls back to `default`, so the inert placeholders can't silently flip), applied via the normalized earliness form engine-wide (resolveCuts measured legs + registry convention thresholds). `label` is a find-me aid (ignored by code). Statically imported -> editing requires a redeploy. NOTE: zero-valued cuts (R1 red 0.0, GT amber 0.0, EURC red 0.0) are IMMOVABLE under the |v|-relative form; each of THESE has a nonzero sibling leg so an override is still meaningful. NVDA is NOT such a case — its only bands are amber 0 (immovable) and red null, so a non-1.0 override is a TOTAL no-op; NVDA is therefore left OUT of REACHABLE_IDS and an override on it THROWS (like F5). A non-1.0 override on an id whose scorer isn't yet wired to consume a multiplier THROWS at validation time (wire the scorer first — docs/reference.md §[indicator] Bands & the threshold multiplier); 1.0 placeholders stay legal.
